title: अंश ५ · अध्याय ३६

items.text:
मेत्रेय!श्रूयतां तस्य बलस्य बलशालिनः ।
कृतं यदन्यत्तेनाभूत्तदपि श्रूयतां द्रिज ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
metreya!śrūyatāṃ tasya balasya balaśālinaḥ |
kṛtaṃ yadanyattenābhūttadapi śrūyatāṃ drija || 1 ||

items.text:
नरकस्यासुरेन्द्रस्य देवपक्षविरोधिनः ।
सखाभवन्महावीर्य्यो द्रिविदो नाम वानरः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
narakasyāsurendrasya devapakṣavirodhinaḥ |
sakhābhavanmahāvīryyo drivido nāma vānaraḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
वैरानुबन्ध बलवान् स चकार सुरान् प्रित ।
नरक हतवान् कृष्णो बलदर्पसमन्वितम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
vairānubandha balavān sa cakāra surān prita |
naraka hatavān kṛṣṇo baladarpasamanvitam || 3 ||

items.text:
करिष्ये सर्व्वदेवानां तस्मादेतत्प्रतिक्रियाम् ।
यज्ञविध्वंसनं कुर्व्वन् मर्त्तलोकक्षयं तथा ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
kariṣye sarvvadevānāṃ tasmādetatpratikriyām |
yajñavidhvaṃsanaṃ kurvvan marttalokakṣayaṃ tathā || 4 ||

items.text:
ततो विध्वसयामास यज्ञानज्ञानमोहितः ।
बिबेद साधुमर्य्यादां क्षयं चक्र च देहिनाम् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tato vidhvasayāmāsa yajñānajñānamohitaḥ |
bibeda sādhumaryyādāṃ kṣayaṃ cakra ca dehinām || 5 ||

items.text:
ददाह च वनोद्देशान् पुरग्रामान्तराणि च ।
क्वचिज्व पर्व्वताक्षेपैर्ग्रामादीन् समचूणोयत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
dadāha ca vanoddeśān puragrāmāntarāṇi ca |
kvacijva parvvatākṣepairgrāmādīn samacūṇoyat || 6 ||

items.text:
शैलानुतूपाट्य तोयेषु मुमोचाम्बुनिधौ तथा ।
पुनञ्चार्णवमध्यस्थः क्षोभयामास सागरम् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
śailānutūpāṭya toyeṣu mumocāmbunidhau tathā |
punañcārṇavamadhyasthaḥ kṣobhayāmāsa sāgaram || 7 ||

items.text:
तेन विक्षोभितश्वाब्धिरुद्रेलोऽजायत द्रिज ।
प्लावयंस्तीरजान् ग्रामान् पुरादीनतिवेगवान् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tena vikṣobhitaśvābdhirudrelo'jāyata drija |
plāvayaṃstīrajān grāmān purādīnativegavān || 8 ||

items.text:
कामरूपी महारूपं कृत्वा संस्थानशेषतः ।
लुण्ठन् भ्रमणसंमर्द्देः सञ्चूर्णायति वानरः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
kāmarūpī mahārūpaṃ kṛtvā saṃsthānaśeṣataḥ |
luṇṭhan bhramaṇasaṃmarddeḥ sañcūrṇāyati vānaraḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
तेन विप्रकृतं सर्व्वं जगदेतदूदुरात्मना ।
निः स्वाध्यायवषटूकारं मैत्रेयासीत् सुदुः खितम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tena viprakṛtaṃ sarvvaṃ jagadetadūdurātmanā |
niḥ svādhyāyavaṣaṭūkāraṃ maitreyāsīt suduḥ khitam || 10 ||

items.text:
एकदा रैवतोद्याने पपौ पानं हलायुधः ।
रेवती च महाभागा तथैवान्या वरस्त्रियः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
ekadā raivatodyāne papau pānaṃ halāyudhaḥ |
revatī ca mahābhāgā tathaivānyā varastriyaḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
उपगीयमानो विलसल्ललनामौलिमध्यगः ।
रेमे यदुवरश्वष्ठः कुवेर इव मन्दरे ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
upagīyamāno vilasallalanāmaulimadhyagaḥ |
reme yaduvaraśvaṣṭhaḥ kuvera iva mandare || 12 ||

items.text:
ततः स वानरोऽभ्येत्य गृहीत्वा सीरिणो हलम् ।
मुषलञ्च चकारास्य सम्मुख़्च बिड़म्बनम् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa vānaro'bhyetya gṛhītvā sīriṇo halam |
muṣalañca cakārāsya sammuḵhca biṛambanam || 13 ||

items.text:
तथैव योषितां तासां जहासाभिमुखं कपिः ।
पानपूर्णाश्व करकांश्विक्षेपाहत्य वै तदा ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
tathaiva yoṣitāṃ tāsāṃ jahāsābhimukhaṃ kapiḥ |
pānapūrṇāśva karakāṃśvikṣepāhatya vai tadā || 14 ||

items.text:
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा भर्तूसयामास तं बलः ।
तथापि तमवज्ञाय चक्र किलकिलाध्वनिम् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ kopaparītātmā bhartūsayāmāsa taṃ balaḥ |
tathāpi tamavajñāya cakra kilakilādhvanim || 15 ||

items.text:
ततः समुत्थाय बलो जग्राह मुषल रुषा ।
सोऽपि शैलशिलां भीमां जग्राह प्लवगोत्तमः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ samutthāya balo jagrāha muṣala ruṣā |
so'pi śailaśilāṃ bhīmāṃ jagrāha plavagottamaḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
चिक्षेप च स तां क्षिप्तां मुषलेन सहस्त्रधा ।
बिभेद यादवश्वेष्ठः सा पपात महीतले ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
cikṣepa ca sa tāṃ kṣiptāṃ muṣalena sahastradhā |
bibheda yādavaśveṣṭhaḥ sā papāta mahītale || 17 ||

items.text:
आपतन्मुषलञ्चासौ समुल्लङ्घय प्लवङ्गमः ।
वेगेनागम्य रोषेण तलेनोरस्यताड़यत् ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
āpatanmuṣalañcāsau samullaṅghaya plavaṅgamaḥ |
vegenāgamya roṣeṇa talenorasyatāṛayat || 18 ||

items.text:
ततो बलेन कोपेन मुष्टिना मूद्धि ताड़ितः ।
पपात रुधिरोदूगारी द्रिविदः क्षीणाजीवितः ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
tato balena kopena muṣṭinā mūddhi tāṛitaḥ |
papāta rudhirodūgārī drividaḥ kṣīṇājīvitaḥ || 19 ||

items.text:
पतता तच्छरीरेण गिरेः श्वृङ्गमदीर्य्यत ।
मैत्रेय!शतधा वज्रिवजणेव हि ताड़ितम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
patatā taccharīreṇa gireḥ śvṛṅgamadīryyata |
maitreya!śatadhā vajrivajaṇeva hi tāṛitam || 20 ||

items.text:
पुष्पवृष्टिं ततो देवा रामस्योपरि चिक्षिपुः ।
प्रशशंसुस्तथाभ्येत्य साध्वेतत्ते महत् कृतम् ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ tato devā rāmasyopari cikṣipuḥ |
praśaśaṃsustathābhyetya sādhvetatte mahat kṛtam || 21 ||

items.text:
अनेन दुष्टकपिना दैत्यपक्षोपकारिणा ।
जगन्निराकृतं वीर! दिष्ट्यासौ क्षयमागतः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
anena duṣṭakapinā daityapakṣopakāriṇā |
jagannirākṛtaṃ vīra! diṣṭyāsau kṣayamāgataḥ || 22 ||

items.text: इत्युक्त्वा दिवमाजग्मुर्देवा ह्टष्टाः सगुह्यकाः ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr: ityuktvā divamājagmurdevā hṭaṣṭāḥ saguhyakāḥ || 23 ||

items.text:
एवंविधान्यनेकानि बलदेवस्य धीमतः ।
कर्म्माण्यपरिमेयाणि शेषस्य धरणीबृतः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃvidhānyanekāni baladevasya dhīmataḥ |
karmmāṇyaparimeyāṇi śeṣasya dharaṇībṛtaḥ || 24 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Listen, O Maitreya, to another achievement accomplished by the powerful Balarāma. The great Asura, Naraka, the enemy of the friends of the celestials, had a friend of exceeding might in a monkey named Dwivida, who was worked up with implacable hostility against the celestials, and vowed to revenge on all of them the destruction of Naraka by Krishna at the instigation of the king of the celestials, by preventing sacrifices and bringing about the total destruction of the world. Blinded by ignorance therefore, he interrupted all religious practices, put down all righteous observances, and brought about the death of living creatures; he set fire to forests, to villages and towns; sometimes he deluged cities and villages with a downpour of rocks or lifting up mountains in the waters he cast them into the ocean; then placing himself in the midst of the deep, he agitated the waves until the foaming sea rose above its confines and swept away the villages and cities situated upon its shores. Dwivida, who was capable of assuming shapes as he liked, enlarged his bulk to an immense proportion, and rolling and tumbling and trampling amidst the corn-fields, he crushed and spoiled the harvest. The whole world, disorganised by this vicious monkey, was deprived of sacred study and religious ceremonies, and was greatly afflicted.

Once on a time Halāyudha was drinking in the groves of Raivata along with the illustrious Revati and other beautiful females; and the celebrated Yadu whose glories were sung and who was pre-eminent amidst graceful and sportive women, resembled Kuvera, the god of riches, in his palace. In the meantime, the monkey Dwivida came there and stealing the ploughshare and the club of Balarāma, grinned at and mocked him, and laughed at the women and threw over and broke the cups filled with wine. Enraged at this, Balarāma threatened the monkey; but the latter disregarded his threats and chattering noise. Thereupon Balarāma started up and seized his club in anger, and the monkey laid hold of a large rock which he hurled at the hero. And casting his club at it as it approached him, Bala broke it into a thousand pieces, which together with the club, fell upon the ground. Beholding the club thus fallen, the monkey sprang over it and struck the Yādava violently on the breast with his paws. Bala returned it with a blow of his fist upon the fore-head of Dwivida which felled him, vomiting blood and lifeless to the earth. The crest of the mountain on which he fell was sundered into a hundred pieces by the weight of his body, as if the Thunderer had shivered it with his thunder-bolt. The celestials threw down a shower of flowers upon Rāma and approached him and praised him for the glorious feat he had performed.

"Well has the world been freed" said they "by thy prowess, O hero, of his vile ape, who was the enemy of the celestials". Then well pleased, they and their attendant spirits returned to heaven. Many such inimitable deeds were performed by the illustrious Baladeva, the impersonation of Sesha, the supporter of the earth.
